full_judgment:
2. Facts, relevant for disposal of this Rule, in brief, are that, one Miss Jakia Begum, as plaintiff, had filed Title Suit No.553 of 2011 before the court of Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, against the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Com-missioner, Dhaka, seeking declaration that recording of the property mentioned in the schedule to the plaint in the Maganagar Khatin No. 1 of Mouza Ramanandapur, PS Adabor, District: Dhaka is wrong and illegal. It also appears that, the Government has acquired the land on 12-12-1984 and subsequently handed over the possession to Mohammadpur Housing PC Culture Farming Co-operative Society, vide deed No. 944 dated 21-4-1985. Thereafter, the said property was developed and divided into several plots, keeping necessary amenities, roads etc. Subsequently, by a registered deed of allotment No. 980 dated 3-3-1987, the suit Plot No. 44, Road No. 6, Block—Kha comprises 2.50 Katha of land were allotted to the plaintiff and possession of the same was handed over to the plaintiff but, during City Jorip, the said Plot No.44 was changed to Plot No. 2951 comprising 0.0408 acres of land which were recorded in Khatian No. 1, in the name of the Government, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka (Exhibit 3). Hence, being aggrieved, the plaintiff has filed this suit. 

 3. The Government appeared in the suit by filing written statements on 29-7-2012 and denying the title and possession of the plaintiff without assigning any cogent reason or without justification as to why the suit property was recorded in the disputed Khatian No. 1 (Exhibit 3). However, the plaintiff has adduced oral and documentary evidences in support of her case, while the defendant did not produce any evidence in support of its title except a letter of authority dated 20-4-2014, submitted by an Assistant Commissioner of land (Exhibit-Ka) and a Khatian No. 1 of Dhaka City Survey, marked as Exhibit 'Kha' respectively. In Khatian No. 1 (Exhibit-Kha), the disputed property has been shown to have been recorded in the name of the Government. I, however, do not find any documents of title in favour of the Government to authorize it to prepare such a Khatian in its name. 

 8. Learned Advocates Mr Sheikh Mohammed Serajul Islam along with Mrs Lucky Ahmed appeared on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1-4. Mr Islam submits that, it is admitted fact that, the suit property along with other adjacent properties were acquired by the Government on 12-12-1994 by way of acquisition and the said property was handed over to the Mohammadpur Housing PC Culture Farming Co-operative Society, vide deed No. 944 dated 21-4-1985, and subsequently, by a registered deed of allotment No. 980 dated 3-3-1987, the suit Plot No. 44, Road No. 6, Block—Kha comprises 2.50 Katha of land were allotted to the plaintiff and the said Housing Society, vide registered deed of allotment dated 3-3-1987 handed over the possession to the plaintiff. He further submits that, the plaintiff herself had appeared and deposed before the court and proved the document of title, Exhibit 2. He next submits that, one Md Enamul Haque, deposed as PW 1 and he has proved the case of the plaintiff by adducing all necessary documents, vide the attested photocopy of the DCR mutation case whereby khatian has been opened in the name of the plaintiff, which are still lying in the LCR, but the same were not exhibited, since these are the photocopies. Both the courts below have taken notice and the defendant could not deny the genuineness of this document, filed by the plaintiff. In addition to that, the plaintiff has submitted the City Corporation holding Tax payment receipts No. 17977 dated 28-2-2014, in original issued by Dhaka North City Corporation to prove her possession in the suit property. The trial court had examined all these documents and had passed the judgment and decree in favour of the plaintiff, which the defendant ought to have complied with instead of causing further harassment to the litigant, who is bearing cost of her own litigation. But, the defendant preferred Title Appeal No. No.483 of 2016 without any genuine ground, by abusing public fund, and has lost in that appeal as well. He then submits that, the appellate court has also passed the impugned judgment and decree dated 10-10-2017 (decree signed on 17-10-2017), after himself examining the evidence on record oral and documentary, and discussed all the relevant issues, independently, dismissed the appeal. It is the admitted case of the plaintiff that, she is the owner and possessor of the suit property and a clear mistake was done by the concerned person, who had wrongly recorded the plaintiff's property in khatian No. 1. The plaintiff's witnesses have consistently proved the case and the plaintiff has adduced oral and documentary evidences before the court, which the defendant could not deny, and, as such, in passing the impugned judgment and decree, the appellate court has committed no error of law, nor there is any case of misreading or non-reading of evidence, nor any case of occasioning any failure of justice. This application, he submits, is simply causing harassment to the plaintiff by using public money and economic hardship upon the plaintiff either to secure unlawful gain or for other reasons better known to them, while this revisional application has been filed after causing delay of 308 days. He next submits that, the Government side could not produce anything to show as to how and where the courts below have committed error of law and as to why the concurrent findings of the courts below should be interfered with Therefore, he proceeds on that, this Rule has no merit and the same may kindly be discharged with exemplary cost. 

 10. It is admitted fact that, the suit property along with other adjacent properties were acquired by the Government on 12-12-1994 by way of acquisition and the said property was handed over to the Mohammadpur Housing PC Culture Farming Co-operative Society, vide deed No. 944 dated 21-4-1985 and subsequently, by a registered deed of allotment No. 980 dated 3-3-1987, the suit Plot No. 44, Road No. 6, Block—Kha comprises 2.50 Katha of land were allotted to the plaintiff and the Housing Society, vide registered deed of allotment dated 3-3-1987, has been handed over to the plaintiff. The plaintiff herself deposed before the court and proved the document of title, marked as Exhibit 2, while one Md Enamul Haque, deposed as PW 1, has corroborated the case of the plaintiff by adducing all necessary documents, vide the attested photocopy of the DCR mutation case, whereby khatian has been opened in the name of the plaintiff, which are still lying in the LCR, but the same were not exhibited, since these are the photocopies and prepared by the Government attaching presumption under section 114 of the Evidence Act. Both the courts below have taken notice and the defendant could not deny the genuineness of these documents, filed by the plaintiff. In addition to that, the plaintiff has submitted City Corporation holding Tax payment receipts No. 17977 dated 28-2-2014 in original, issued by Dhaka North City Corporation, to prove her possession in the suit property. The trial court has examined all these documents and had passed the judgment and decree in favour of the plaint, which the defendant ought to have complied with instead of causing harassment to the litigant at the cost of public fund and by abusing the official position as a public servant, in a case like the instant one. Rather, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, representing the Government, preferred Title Appeal No. No.483 of 2016, without any genuine cause and has lost in that appeal as well. The appellate court has also passed the impugned judgment and decree dated 10-10-2017 (decree signed on 17-10-2017), after himself examining the evidence on record oral, and documentary, and having discussed all the relevant facts and issues, independently, he has dismissed the appeal. It is the admitted case of the plaintiff that, she is the owner and possessor of the suit property and a clear mistake was done by the concerned person, who was wrongly recorded her plot in the khatian No.1. 

 13. This Court hereby declared the law, within the meaning of Article 111 of the Constitution of the Peoples' Republic of Bangladesh that is binding upon the Government as per Article 112 of the Constitution that, the question of possession of the property is miserably related to the question of title in the suit property. In anybody lacks lawful title in any property, then his or her obtaining and remaining in possession in that property or to get his/her name recorded in the khatain do not arise. The staffs working in the field survey operation cannot be indulged in the owner of a property shall remain standing in that place like a tree. In so many cases, owner of the property may not live in the property and he may stay at any other places or even in the abroad, but that does not authorizes a Government staff working in the field to record name of other person because of physical absence of the owner, when any title or other document to show that the Government has any right, title in the suit property is wanting. In order to write name of the Government in any khas khatian, the Government should or have some kind of document of title or some legal basis for claiming it as khas property of the Government, acquired by it or otherwise vested in it. Here, the person of the Government is as equal as any other ordinary person. The Government must have some basis or documents or other lawful sources to claim title in the concerned land in order to record its name in the khas khatian.
